General.Description:
The year is 1923. The war is over, the empires are cracking at their edges, and the skies above the Mediterranean belong to whoever is fast enough and bold enough to claim them. The Meridian — three hundred metres of armour-plated airship, crewed by forty-six of the most ungovernable people in the known world — has been claiming them for seven years.

When engineer Petra Voss is shanghaied aboard the Meridian after her prototype navigation system is stolen at a Vienna airshow, she expects imprisonment. What she gets is an offer: join the crew, help us find the stolen system, and keep sixty percent of whatever we recover from the vault of the man who took it.

The Sky Pirates is a breathless, funny, and thoroughly charming adventure novel set in a gorgeously realised alternative 1920s Europe where airship travel is the dominant mode of long-distance transport and the gaps between nations are controlled by private fleets of extraordinary audacity. Luna Vega writes her ensemble cast with warm precision — every crew member of the Meridian is fully three-dimensional — and her action sequences have a kinetic, cinematic quality that makes them irresistible.

Joyous from first page to last.
